key_insight: An online evolutionary machine-learning approach can better handle neural activity drift and improve long-term seizure prediction from continuous intracranial EEG than standard offline testing.
clinical_relevance: This could support more realistic seizure-prediction systems for drug-resistant epilepsy, but it is still a research framework rather than a ready-to-use clinical tool.
method: Built the first public continuous long-term sEEG dataset for seizure prediction: 16 patients, 664.9 hours, 121 seizures.
Compared offline pipeline choices, then tested the best setup in a pseudo-prospective online setting under realistic class imbalance.
Evolved 1,000 candidate models per patient and reduced input channels using patient-specific epileptogenic network estimation.
evidence_signal: Offline AUROC dropped from 90% to 57.9% in online evaluation, while the evolutionary framework achieved complete event-level prediction in 75% of patients and predicted all but one seizure in 87.5%.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated in a proof-of-concept retrospective/online simulation, so real-world prospective validation and workflow integration are still needed.
paper_title: Countering Neural Activity Drift: Sustained Long-term Seizure Prediction Using an Evolutionary Machine-Learning Framework on Continuous Intracranial EEG
